title: Tracepack Evidence Interchange v1
description: A portable evidence payload an external producer hands to Tracepack. See SPEC.md in this package for the full design and the meaning of every field, especially the trust boundary around `observations` and the two separate hash concepts. This is the canonical, language-agnostic contract — packages/evidence-interchange/src/types.ts and validate.ts are its TypeScript mirror, kept in sync and checked against shared fixtures in tests/.

schema_version.description: Required from v1 onward. An importer must reject any schema_version it does not explicitly support before interpreting anything else in the payload.

producer_id.description: Stable machine identifier, producer-chosen. Reverse-DNS style recommended, e.g. "com.example.review-analyzer".

producer_name.description: Human-readable name shown in Tracepack's UI and exports.

capture_timestamp.description: ISO 8601, when the PRODUCER captured or generated this evidence — not when Tracepack imports it.

source_url.description: Absolute http(s) URL this evidence relates to, if applicable.

evidence_type.description: Producer-defined free-text classification, e.g. "product_listing_review". Not a closed enum — Tracepack does not gatekeep what kinds of evidence exist.

attachments.description: May be empty — see SPEC.md section 6.3 for how an attachment-less payload is represented in Tracepack.

observations.description: Claims made by the producer named in `source`, which is itself self-asserted and not cryptographically verified — see SPEC.md sections 4 and 5. Tracepack does not independently verify these claims either — see SPEC.md section 4 for how this trust boundary is preserved through import and export.

metadata.description: Producer-defined open extension point. Serialised size is capped at 64KB and must not contain __proto__, constructor, or prototype keys at any depth.

canonicalization.description: RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme), unmodified — see SPEC.md section 6.2 for the exact field-exclusion rule and worked test vectors.

payload_hash.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the payload, excluding attachments[].data and this field itself. Proves the structured claims were not altered relative to what was hashed — does NOT prove they are true, and does NOT prove who computed the hash. See SPEC.md sections 5 and 13.

mime_type.description: Deliberately limited to the MIME types Tracepack can already preview, embed and export today.

size.description: Decoded byte length. The importer verifies this against the actual decoded size and rejects a mismatch.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the attachment's original binary file bytes, computed BEFORE base64 encoding (never of the base64 text itself). Proves the bytes Tracepack stored match what the producer sent — does not prove the attachment is authentic, or who sent it. See SPEC.md section 6.1 for the exact procedure and a worked test vector.

encoding.description: The only transport v1 supports. No remote URI references and no multipart bundles — see SPEC.md section 7 for why this is a deliberate scope decision, not an oversight.

kind.description: Producer-defined observation type, e.g. "suspicious_review_clustering". Not a closed enum.

confidence.description: The PRODUCER's own confidence in this claim, not a Tracepack-assigned score.

attachment_ref.description: If set, must match an attachments[].id in this same payload. If absent, this observation is about the evidence as a whole.

data.description: Producer-defined open extension point, same 64KB / unsafe-key limits as top-level metadata.
